content.rationale: Bottleneck Mahalanobis distance is sensitive to near-OOS intent shifts, while pooled encoder distance captures broader domain shifts. Training-set robust scaling makes their additive fusion comparable without using evaluation-set statistics.

ViM-style residual norm measures how much an encoder representation lies outside the principal in-scope feature subspace. Combining this train-calibrated residual with energy captures both representation-space novelty and classifier uncertainty.
Distance to nearby training examples within the classifier's predicted intent measures whether a query is locally compatible with that intent, rather than merely close to any in-scope class.

OOS queries can deviate along low-variance within-class directions that are largely ignored by principal-subspace distances. The trailing-eigenspace score measures these atypical residual variations using a subspace fitted only on in-scope training features.

A query can be close to an in-scope class overall yet be atypical for the class selected by the classifier. Predicted-class Mahalanobis distance, calibrated against that class's training-distance tail, exposes this classifier-feature mismatch.

OOS inputs often produce less decisive separation between the largest and second-largest logits. Calibrating the top-two margin within each predicted class accounts for intent-specific confidence scales using training logits only.
L2-normalized class prototypes measure angular compatibility with in-scope intents, so low maximum cosine similarity identifies queries whose feature direction is atypical.

Trailing-subspace distance detects atypical low-variance feature residuals, while MSP captures classifier uncertainty. Robust train-fitted scaling makes these complementary signals comparable without using evaluation-set statistics.

Dirichlet differential entropy uses the full concentration shape, assigning higher scores to broad and weakly concentrated evidential posteriors rather than relying only on total evidence. This can flag OOS inputs whose evidence is diffuse across intents.

This gate preserves energy ranking for confident in-scope-like predictions, but progressively relies on pooled-feature Mahalanobis distance when energy indicates uncertainty. The gate and both score scales are calibrated only from training items.

A shrunk diagonal covariance for each intent preserves intent-specific feature scales while avoiding unstable full class covariances. OOS queries should have low likelihood under every class-specific diagonal Gaussian.
A supervised class-mean subspace retains directions that distinguish known intents, so a large residual orthogonal to that subspace indicates variation unexplained by in-scope intent structure.

Bottleneck and pooled Mahalanobis densities capture complementary near-OOS and far-OOS shifts. A train-fitted covariance-aware additive weighting downweights redundant density signals without using evaluation statistics.
The norm outside the principal in-scope encoder subspace measures representation variation not explained by dominant training-feature structure, which should increase for OOS queries.

A query should be closer to examples that the classifier assigns to the same intent than to the training set globally. The ratio of prediction-conditioned to global local distance flags classifier-feature mismatches characteristic of near-OOS inputs.

Low-variance directions of the pooled within-class covariance expose subtle deviations that dominant representation directions can hide. Conditioning the residual on the classifier's predicted intent flags inputs that are atypical for the intent the model assigns.

In-scope examples should be substantially closer to one class mean than to competing class means. OOS queries often have a smaller nearest-versus-runner-up Mahalanobis gap, indicating ambiguous compatibility with known intents.

The centered logit norm measures overall predictive sharpness independently of an additive logit offset. A two-sided, predicted-class-conditioned calibration flags both unusually diffuse and unusually overconfident logit shapes that are atypical of in-scope examples.

Class-conditional cosine similarity measures angular compatibility with the intent predicted by the classifier. Calibrating similarity against that intent's in-scope training tail flags examples whose representation is atypical for their assigned class.

MSP captures classifier uncertainty while pooled-space Mahalanobis distance captures representation novelty. Empirical train CDF calibration puts both signals on a comparable tail-probability scale before combining them.

The normalized Dirichlet concentration pattern has an intent-specific shape that is distinct from total evidence or energy. Queries with unusually diffuse or unusually uneven concentration shapes relative to their predicted intent receive high scores.

For confidently classified queries, the score remains the model energy; only in the train-calibrated uncertain-energy region does unusually large pooled-feature distance add evidence for OOS. Centering feature distance by its expected value at the same energy prevents representation novelty that is typical of uncertain in-scope items from being over-penalized.

A prediction-conditioned diagonal Mahalanobis score retains intent-specific feature variances while shrinkage stabilizes rare intents. Calibrating each predicted intent's distance against its own in-scope distance distribution exposes queries that the classifier assigns confidently but whose representation is atypical for that intent.

A ridge map from pooled features to training logits identifies representation directions that the classifier actually uses to separate known intents. Large residual energy outside this logit-discriminative subspace indicates feature variation unsupported by in-scope decisions.

A ViM-style virtual-class probability compares the residual component outside the train principal feature subspace against the classifier's known-class logit evidence. OOS queries should have a stronger residual-derived virtual logit while retaining sensitivity to their classifier confidence.

A multiview local-neighborhood score averages angular distance in pooled encoder space and bottleneck space, so OOS inputs are flagged when they lack close in-scope semantic neighbors in either representation.

Trailing within-class covariance directions capture subtle representation deviations that dominant semantic directions can obscure. A predicted-intent-conditioned training tail calibration flags samples unusually displaced in those low-variance directions.

A query assigned to an intent should be close to that intent's Gaussian mean, and that assigned intent should not be much worse than the closest feature-space intent. Class-conditioned calibration of predicted-class novelty and classifier-feature disagreement highlights atypical assignments without using evaluation-set statistics.

The relative isolation of the winning logit from the runner-up, compared with competition among the next classes, captures logit geometry beyond energy or maximum probability. Class-prediction-conditioned two-sided tail calibration flags unusually ambiguous or unusually isolated known-class decisions.

L2-normalized pooled representations of in-scope queries should align with their nearest class prototype. Low maximum cosine similarity to normalized class prototypes indicates weak angular compatibility with known intents.

Energy and pooled-space Mahalanobis novelty capture complementary classifier uncertainty and representation mismatch. Train empirical CDF calibration puts their upper-tail evidence on a shared scale before combining them.

After removing the predicted intent's concentration, the relative allocation of Dirichlet mass across competing intents forms an intent-specific confusion profile. OOS inputs can have atypical alternative-intent evidence patterns even when their total evidence and vacuity appear in-distribution.

Energy is retained for clearly in-distribution logit patterns, while samples in the train-calibrated uncertain-energy tail are softly switched toward pooled-space novelty. Conditioning the Mahalanobis tail rank on an energy stratum prevents naturally uncertain in-scope queries from being penalized merely for having larger feature distances.
A heteroscedastic diagonal Mahalanobis distance lets each intent retain its own feature-scale profile while shrinkage prevents small classes from producing unstable variances.

The class-mean subspace contains representation directions that separate known intents. After removing that discriminative component, OOS queries should have weak local support among in-scope residual patterns.

OOS queries can contain encoder variation outside the dominant in-scope representation subspace. Combining PCA residual magnitude with energy preserves classifier uncertainty while adding a feature-space novelty signal.

A query should have several nearby examples from the intent it is predicted to belong to, not merely one accidental neighbor. Prediction-conditioned average k-nearest-neighbor distance captures weak local in-scope support while avoiding cross-intent neighbors.

Each predicted intent has its own low-variance within-class directions after a shared semantic projection. OOS queries should exhibit unusually large standardized residuals along these tightly constrained directions even when broad semantic variation looks familiar.

OOS representations should be both far from their closest known-intent prototype and weakly separated between the nearest competing prototypes. Dividing nearest-class distance by the nearest-versus-runner-up distance emphasizes this prototype ambiguity without using evaluation-set calibration.

Known intents have class-specific logit shapes: their winning-versus-runner-up margin, centered logit norm, and tempered evidence tend to occupy a compact region. A query with an atypical combination of confidence scale and competition structure receives a larger conditional shape distance.

Predicted-intent-conditioned empirical tail probabilities place energy and Gaussian feature novelty on a common train-calibrated scale. A Fisher-style combination raises OOS scores when either logit evidence or representation compatibility is unusually weak for the assigned intent.

The normalized Dirichlet concentration shape has characteristic entropy and dominance for each known intent. A class-conditioned distance in this shape space flags unusually uniform or unusually concentrated evidence allocations without being a monotone function of vacuity.

Energy remains the score for confidently in-scope-like items, while a train-calibrated smooth gate increasingly adds pooled-space Mahalanobis novelty only in the uncertain energy tail. This avoids broadly penalizing confident known-intent queries for benign feature variation.

Known intents should remain compatible with their own coordinate-wise feature variation, including their most constrained representation directions. A class-specific shrunk diagonal tail-residual score detects inputs that violate several tight intent-specific constraints.

Class-mean directions capture encoder variation that discriminates known intents, while large residual energy in their orthogonal complement indicates semantic content unexplained by the intent taxonomy.

A ViM-style virtual OOS logit is proportional to feature energy outside the principal in-scope subspace. Inputs with large residual semantic content receive a larger virtual-class posterior even when their ordinary logits are confident.

A predicted intent should have substantially denser same-intent support than the unrestricted in-scope neighborhood. OOS queries often have nearby training examples only across mixed intents, producing a large class-conditional-to-global distance ratio.

Trailing shared within-class covariance directions encode constraints that in-scope examples rarely violate. Calibrating this residual energy separately for the classifier-predicted intent avoids a globally monotone duplicate of an unconditioned trailing-eigenspace score.

The top-two margin normalized by centered logit scale measures relative winner separation rather than raw confidence. Calibrating this quantity per intent makes unusually weak competition margins receive higher OOS scores.

Known queries should align with the prototype of the class predicted by the classifier. Standardizing predicted-class cosine alignment by that intent's training distribution flags atypical semantic directions while accounting for class-specific prototype spread.

Energy and pooled-space Mahalanobis novelty are converted to train-calibrated upper-tail percentiles before a geometric fusion, so queries that are jointly unusual in classifier evidence and representation compatibility receive the largest OOS scores.
EDL out-of-scope inputs can distribute non-vacuous evidence more evenly across competing intents, creating high evidential dissonance even when total concentration is not unusual.

Classifier energy is retained for training-calibrated confident regions, while smoothly switching to pooled-space Gaussian novelty in the uncertain energy tail. This lets representation distance resolve cases where logits provide weak OOS separation.

A predicted intent should assign a representation a typical class-conditional diagonal likelihood after accounting for that intent's own coordinate variances. Shrinkage and per-class train-calibrated surprise avoid favoring broad intents merely because they have larger spread.

After removing the span of class-mean directions that explain intent-discriminative variation, in-scope queries should retain locally supported residual semantic directions. OOS queries often contain residual content not represented by nearby training examples.

Bottleneck and pooled representations capture complementary novelty: the bottleneck is sensitive to deviations near learned intent boundaries, while pooled encoder features capture broader semantic shifts. Predicted-intent-conditioned density surprises are standardized on training data and combined with train-fitted weights based on how well each space distinguishes training prediction errors.

In-scope encoder representations should be well explained by a principal subspace learned from training features. A large fraction of energy in the orthogonal residual space indicates semantic content outside the learned intent manifold.

Averaging normalized pooled-feature neighborhood radii across short, medium, and broad local scales makes the score less sensitive to a single neighbor while detecting queries that lack consistent semantic support from the in-scope training manifold.

Low-variance within-class directions encode constraints that in-scope examples rarely violate. Class-conditional local support in a whitened trailing-eigenspace detects queries whose subtle residual variation is unsupported by their predicted intent.

A query can be close to some known intent while still being incompatible with the intent selected by the classifier. Predicted-class Mahalanobis surprise flags disagreement between classifier routing and class-conditional representation support.

A temperature-softened top-two logit margin measures ambiguity among the most plausible known intents while reducing sensitivity to absolute logit scale. OOS inputs often have an unusually small winner-versus-runner-up separation compared with training queries.

In-scope queries should align closely with the l2-normalized prototype of the class selected by the classifier. Low predicted-class cosine similarity, calibrated against training examples routed to that class, indicates semantic mismatch with known intent structure.

Classifier energy and predicted-intent representation mismatch capture complementary OOS signals. Converting each to train-fitted normal scores makes their additive fusion insensitive to incompatible raw scales.

OOS inputs can induce Dirichlet concentration profiles that are atypical for the classifier-routed intent, including unusual combinations of total evidence, concentration entropy, and winner separation. A class-conditional profile distance uses the shape of the Dirichlet parameters rather than a score monotone in energy or vacuity.

Energy remains the score for train-calibrated confident queries, while a smooth high-energy gate transfers weight to predicted-intent bottleneck Mahalanobis surprise when classifier evidence is uncertain. This targets examples whose uncertain routing is better resolved by representation compatibility.

Per-intent diagonal variances capture dimensions that are tightly constrained for one intent but variable for another. Predicted-class shrinkage Mahalanobis surprise flags samples that are incompatible with the classifier-routed intent without unstable full covariance inversion.

Class-mean directions explain variation used to discriminate known intents, so residual directions retain within-intent semantic detail. Queries routed to an intent but lacking class-conditional residual neighbors are likely out of scope rather than ordinary examples of that intent.

Rather than using raw residual magnitude, this score measures the fraction of centered feature energy outside a global in-scope principal subspace and calibrates it per routed intent. OOS queries can have atypically large off-subspace semantic content even when their overall feature norm is ordinary.
Bottleneck and pooled embeddings encode complementary notions of local in-scope support. A query that is isolated in either representation space receives a high train-calibrated novelty score.

Low-variance directions of the pooled within-class covariance encode feature changes rarely observed for known intents. Class-conditioned, train-calibrated trailing-subspace energy highlights routed queries that violate these tight semantic constraints while avoiding domination by overall embedding magnitude.

Known intents should occupy relatively distinct Voronoi regions around class-conditional feature means, whereas OOS queries are often similarly distant from multiple intents. A train-calibrated small nearest-versus-second-nearest Mahalanobis separation flags this ambiguity.

Known intents tend to produce a characteristic class-conditional dispersion of centered logits. OOS queries often have unusually compressed relative logit evidence even when their absolute energy is not extreme.

L2-normalized class prototypes summarize the semantic direction of each labeled in-scope intent. A query with unusually low cosine alignment to its routed intent prototype, relative to that intent's training distribution, is more likely OOS.

Energy and pooled-space Mahalanobis distance are converted to train-fitted empirical tail scales before a smooth maximum combines either form of novelty. This preserves strong OOS evidence from representation mismatch even when logit uncertainty is modest, and vice versa.
